title: Clean body, clean place
hookLine: wudu, clean clothes, a clean spot, and the idea behind them

cards: A man rolls up his sleeves at work, in the restroom, and washes his hands, his mouth, his face, his arms to the elbow, wipes his head, washes his feet. A coworker walks in and looks a little puzzled. He's not being fussy.
He's getting ready. Before anyone says a word of the prayer, the cleanness comes first.

teach.b: The Arabic word is taharah, purity or cleanness. Books of Islamic law put it ahead of the chapter on prayer, because the prayer isn't valid without it. It has three layers.

teach.h: THE BODY, THE CLOTHES, THE PLACE.

teach.b: For the daily prayers that usually means wudu, the washing the Qur'an itself describes in Surah al-Ma'idah: wash your faces, and your hands up to the elbows, wipe your heads, and wash your feet up to the ankles.
After some things, like sleep or using the toilet, wudu needs renewing. After others, like sex, a full bath is needed, called ghusl. Second, the clothes: clean of things like urine or blood.
Third, the place: a clean spot to stand on. That's what a prayer rug is for. It isn't holy in itself, just a clean surface you can carry anywhere.

teach.h: THE WHOLE EARTH, A PLACE OF PRAYER.
teach.b: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said, in a hadith in Bukhari, that the whole earth had been made for him a place of prayer and a means of purification. A field, a parking lot, the edge of an airport gate: any clean ground will do.
When there's no water, or water would harm you, there's tayammum: you touch clean earth or dust and wipe your face and hands.
The idea behind it all is in a short hadith in Sahih Muslim: purity is half of faith. Not a rule tacked on to the prayer. Half of the thing itself.
Some scholars read it as outside and inside together: the water on the skin, and the turning of the heart it's meant to go with.

how: Before each prayer, Muslims make sure they are in wudu (the ritual washing of face, arms, head and feet), that their clothes are clean, and that they pray on a clean spot, often a prayer rug; with no water, they use tayammum with clean earth.

o: a set of foods Muslims are allowed to eat
a special robe worn only on festival days
cleanness of body, clothes and place before prayer

games.q: what's inside taharah — tap the pairs.
p: clean earth when there's no water
a clean surface you can carry

s: the prayer rug is holy in itself
it's just a clean surface. the Prophet ﷺ said the whole earth was made a place of prayer.
a hadith calls purity half of faith
it's in Sahih Muslim: purity is half of faith.
with no water, a Muslim can't pray at all
there's tayammum: touching clean earth and wiping the face and hands.

games.q: you need to pray, you're in a field, and there's no water anywhere. what does the tradition say?
o: skip the prayer until you find water
touch clean earth and wipe your face and hands
games.why: tayammum: clean earth stands in for water. the Qur'an allows it, and the hadith says the earth was made a means of purification.

practice: Clear one small spot near you, a corner of the floor, a chair, a patch of desk, and if you have a clean cloth, a towel or a scarf, lay it down flat and smooth it with your hands.
Sit near it, breathing slowly, and look: a small place where nothing is piled up. If you've done wudu before, notice where the water would go; if you pray, this is the kind of place you'd pray on.

wordCard.voice: Taharah. Cleanness of body, clothes and place, the half of faith that comes before the prayer. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: purity, cleanness; the chapter that comes before prayer in books of Islamic law.

carryVoice: Your line: a clean corner. The prayer, step by step, starts here. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Qur'an 5:6 (the washing before prayer, and tayammum)
Sahih Muslim 223 (purity is half of faith)
Sahih al-Bukhari 335 (the earth made a place of prayer and a means of purification)
